coverage: Named on-disk roster: 10/10 FETCHED and fully claimed (they were on disk from an earlier round but NONE of their URLs appeared among the 386 existing verified claims, so all were virgin); note they live under sweep/hobb-raw and sweep/hobb-acad, not the paths the brief gave. Named second routes: Mendlesohn Rhetorics of Fantasy BLOCKED at the primary (archive.org search-inside answers "Item not available" for the lending-restricted item; IA was also intermittently offline) — its relay via Elliott's bibliography was already claimed last round; Mandala NOT FOUND (no accessible full text; Elliott's exhaustive Hobb bibliography carries no Mandala entry); Ekman Here Be Dragons NOT FOUND for Hobb (no Elliott entry either, though Ekman & Taylor on epigraphs is already in the corpus); Oliver "Magic Words, Magic Worlds" REACHED BY PROXY and shown to be a MISATTRIBUTION — a chapter-by-chapter review names thirteen authors and never Hobb, so the brief conflated the McFarland monograph with Oliver's separate Mythlore article on Hobb's epigraphs; Borowska-Szerszun ABSTRACT-ONLY (closed access per both Unpaywall and OpenAlex, absent from the UwB repository); Shropshire NOT FOUND (SHAREOK holds zero Hobb records, ProQuest-only); r/Fantasy AMAs BLOCKED (reddit.com is disallowed to this user agent, reddit's JSON API refuses unauthenticated clients, and three Wayback CDX enumerations for the AMA threads timed out or returned empty); video-essay transcripts FETCHED, 5/5. Substantive sources per route: 10 named on-disk, 5 video transcripts, 1 open-access review, 1 abstract-only record = 17 substantive, 94 claims; 8 further sources read and logged non-substantive (blocked, not found, snippet-only, or vendor). Stopping rule met: Crossref and OpenAlex sweeps both surfaced nothing not already on disk. Best finds: Peter Heck (Asimov's, Feb 1997) names the Farseer chapter epigraphs "a brief historical memoir", the closest thing yet to a settlement-dossier register inside the novels; Chris Morgan (Interzone 98, Aug 1995) is the dissenting contemporary reviewer, who read the prose as historical fiction and thought Hobb was a man; and Hobb's own 2012 statement that a character, not a narrator, "introduces setting, culture, conflict, government, economy".
